title: DHCPv6: Reuse DNS SVCB param parsing code for DNR
description: Refactor DNS and DHCPv6 to share the SVCB param parsing code to be used for DNS SVCB records and DHCPv6 DNR options. Also added an expert field for DNR ADN-only mode (RFC9463 3.1.6)

notes.body:
Ewww.  I follow the refactor, but does it make sense to have the service parameters as their own dissector, maybe a PINO (protocol in name only)?  That would result in filter name changes, but much cleaner dissection logic and field setup.
I don't know enough about the protocols themselves to also know if this could get reuse elsewhere, but I prefer dissection functions to macros.
not big fan also of macro but using the same macro like D(TLS)/SSL and it is ok for me.

I went this route because the svc params come from DNS, but are used in the DNR option in DHCPv4, DHCPv6, and Router Advertisements, and it seemed better to try to reuse the logic. I originally followed the way the ECHCONFIG svcparam is handled with call_dissector() into the TLS code, but it seemed that it just reused the hf variables from TLS instead of packing them "dhcpv6.dnr". It was there that I ran into the macro stuff to share between SSL and DTLS.

@mmann78 If I understand your comment correctly, are you suggesting to use the call_dissector() style that DHCPv6 (and others later) could call, while having the logic remain in the DNS dissector? Or pulling it out completely into something like packet-dns-svcparams.c? Is there a way to do that but still have the filtering stuff appear under the base protocol, or is that not possible (or preferred)? Do you have an example for a PINO that I could follow?
